links.reason: Thirattu 9 says Madurai will not decline (குன்றுதல் உண்டோ) as long as the hill exists (குன்றம் உண்டாகும் அளவு): that is the stock eternity formula, with a pun on குன்று, not a limit set on fame. Read plainly it agrees with Kural 233's பொன்றாது நிற்பது; the teaches turns the hyperbole into a 'term' that bounds fame, which the Tamil does not say.

The shared element is முறையுடை அரசன் செங்கோல் அவையம் against Kural 541's முறை, and the lover drops the idea with யாங்காவதுகொல். The poem is uncertain in sense and says nothing about harm without intent being unjudgeable; the teaches builds a jurisprudential limit on the Kural's procedure from a lover's conceit.

Natrinai 121 sets the doe with her stag (இரலையொடு வதியும்) in the charioteer's 'do not fret' (பரியல்), Akananuru 34 has the hero himself moved by the stag's care (பெருந்தகைக்கு உடைந்த நெஞ்சம்) and urging 'செல்க தேரே'. Same distinctive mullai image, opposite use by speaker; the teaches is specific and true.

Both speak to the friend of his leaving (நீப்பின் / நீங்கின்), and the contrast is real: Kural 1155 asks her to stop him (பிரிவோம்பல்), Kuruntokai 334 asks nothing and names only 'our one sweet life' (ஒருநம் இன்னுயிர்). But the situation is the stock one and the mood contrast is thin; the Kural's death of the woman comes from the commentary, not the couplet.

The shared phrase is real (பொய்யா விளக்கம் / பொய்யா விளக்கே), but 753 is about wealth dispelling an enemy's darkness and 299 about truth for the worthy: different domains, not incompatible claims. The teaches admits it can't show intent and only says the verses 'compete for one title', which is the shared phrase restated.

227 calls Death a fool that cooked its seed (வித்துஅட்டு உண்டனை), 230 likens it to a failing farmer who eats his seed (வீழ்குடி உழவன் வித்து உண்டாஅங்கு), and both argue Death has lost the warrior's future killing (இனியார் மற்றுநின் பசிதீர்ப்போரே / நேரார் பல்லுயிர் பருகி ஆர்குவை). Two poets, two kings, one argument: the teaches holds.

Akananuru 60 'தொண்டி அன்ன எம் ஒண்தொடி ஞெமுக்காதீமோ' warns before harm; Kuruntokai 238 'தொண்டி அன்ன என் நலம் தந்து ... சென்மோ' demands the beauty back. Same Tondi measure, before and after, and the demand-for-return reading is in the Tamil. Small slip: கொண்டனை சென்மோ நின் சூளே is 'take your oath and go', not 'keeping' it.

Patitruppattu 22 names கழிகண்ணோட்டம் beside தெறல் கடுமை among the obstacles to the அறம் தெரி திகிரி, which is the excess Kural 578's condition (கருமம் சிதையாமல் கண்ணோட) guards against. A specific rule-and-instance pair; 'older' is an assumption about date but the substance holds.

Every simile in Kalittokai 120 is of cruelty to the already hurt: அல்லற்பட்டு இருந்தாரை, போர் தொலைந்து இருந்தாரை, வெந்தது ஓர் புண்ணின் கண் வேல், and evening is கூற்று நக்கது போலும். That unfolds Kural 1224's கொலைக்களத்து ஏதிலர், enemies at the place of execution, into a series; the teaches is specific.

Matti's Kazhar is named in both (கைவண்மத்தி கழாஅர் அன்ன நல்லோர்; பல்வேல் மத்தி கழாஅர் முன்துறை), a real puram-name connection. But in Ainkurunuru 61 the town is only the measure of the women's excellence, like any town simile, and Akananuru 226 is the friend's speech, not the wife's; 'shorthand for the husband's other women' is not shown.

The echo is real: பெரியோர்ப் பேணி (Patitruppattu 79.3) against பெரியாரைப் பேணித் தமராக் கொளல் (Kural 443). The teaches only observes that the poem lists the trait with சிறியோரை அளித்தி among other virtues; neither verse develops the other, and the pair is close to a shared phrase.

Purananuru 158 says Ori ruled Kolli (கொல்லி ஆண்ட) among the seven now dead; Natrinai 346 calls it பொறையன் பெருந்தண் கொல்லி. Two lords for one hill is a real puram-name finding, but the poems give no order between them, and the akam poem does nothing with the name beyond the kulavi epithet. 'Qualifies' does not fit.

தமவும் பிறவும் ஒப்ப நாடி (Pattinappalai 209) is close to the Kural's பிறவும் தமபோல், and line 210 (கொள்வதூஉம் மிகைகொளாது கொடுப்பதூஉம் குறைகொடாது) adds the test at the scale. The agreement is specific; 'first ... before' assumes the idyll's priority, and the port is not named in this span, but the core holds.

The two words are shared (தொடர்பு, தேயுமோ / தேயுமே), and Kuruntokai 42 does use the moon's verb. But nothing in the poem invokes the great/small distinction: 'காமம் ஒழிவதாயினும் ... தேயுமோ' asserts the bond will outlast desire. Making it a demand that he prove himself one of the great is a generous reading.

Kuruntokai 151 refuses the road (இறப்பல் என்பது ... இளமைக்கு முடிவே); Akananuru 337 is a heart that once turned back (அவணதாகப் பொருள்) and is pressing again. Both are the stock செலவழுங்குதல் situation, and the point that refusal must be remade is already in Akananuru 337's colophon and lines alone.

Thinaimalai 54 asks him to call the sign-readers and fix a day (குறியறிவார்க் கூஉய் ... நாள் நாடி); Akananuru 86 remembers a wedding day when the moon was free of the planet (கோள்கால் நீங்கிய). Auspicious timing of marriage is shared topic; the teaches identifies the two days as one. Note Thinaimalai's 'ஓரில் ஓர் கோள்நாடல் வேண்டா' may itself mean 'no need to search the planets', which would cut against the pairing.

Both quote the friend's denial with என்றி (காரன் றென்றி; பருவந்தான் பட்டின்றே என்றி). Kuruntokai 148 answers with the konrai and kurundham ('கனவோ'), Thinaimalai 103 with the cost: கண்ணீரால் அட்டினேன் ஆவி. The development is specific and the Tamil carries it.

Both are the friend's dissuasion, a stock situation. Ainkurunuru 285's வீங்குவளை நெகிழப் பிரிதல் names the slipping bangle as what his parting would cause, so the teaches' 'wasting already begun' is untrue; and the Kural's speaker is the friend only for Parimelazhagar.

In Kuruntokai 312 the man narrates both disguises of his இரண்டறி கள்வி, so he plainly sees through her; the concealment (தமரோ ரன்னள் வைகறையானே) is aimed at her kin. Kural 1271's eyes speak to the lover. Different audiences, so no incompatible claim, and the teaches' 'a disguise he cannot see through' misdescribes the poem.

Kural 1311 refuses the chest for the slightest offence, being looked at (கண்ணின் பொது உண்பர்); Thinaimalai 152 has the marks printed on it (இட்ட குறி) and puts the refusal (வேண்டா தழூஉம்) under care for his garland, the son's mouth and her milk. Same refusal sharpened in two directions; the teaches holds, though her refusal itself is stated, only the charge is indirect.

Kuruntokai 376 praises a body cool as Pothiyil sandal in summer and warm in the cold (வேனிலானே தண்ணியள்); Ainthinai Aimpathu 24 answers that the shoulders once சந்தனச்சாந்து are now காரத்தின் வெய்ய 'இப்பருவம்'. The sandal figure is shared and turned; the teaches is specific.

The line ஆசா கெந்தை யாண்டுளன் கொல்லோ is shared verbatim, and the context does change its charge: 176 follows his humble words and departure, 325 follows her own 'மன்னிக் கழிக என்றேனே'. The observation is good, but neither verse limits the other: this is a shared formula, so same_image.

Both are a dissuading speech, but Thinaimozhi 12's speaker is unmarked (thurai -) and the Kural's is the friend only by Parimelazhagar. The contrast of tactics, a threat (வாழ்வார்க் குரை) against an appeal to his knowledge (நும்மின் தெரிவார்யார்), is true but thin, and neither develops the other.

Same poet, same eyes (பல்லிதழ் உண்கண்), the neythal spoiled in both: the gull tears it (சிதைக்கும்), the reapers cut it in clearing (மாற்றினர் அறுக்கும்). The gull's 'appetite' is not in the Tamil, so the appetite/indifference contrast in the teaches rests on an added motive.

The closing phrase அவர் தேர்மணிக் குரலே is identical. In Natrinai 145 it comes softly at midnight to a suspicious mother's street; in Ainkurunuru 102 (தாய்க்கு உரைத்த பத்து) it is told to the mother as ringing to end grief (துன்புறு துயரம் நீங்க இன்புற இசைக்கும்). The change of meaning with disclosure is in the Tamil.

The red-eyed buffalo breaking its tie (நோன் தளை பரிந்து / உழலை முருக்கிய) and grazing the field is used against the husband at the door in Akananuru 46 and sent through the bard to the women (பெண்டிர்க்கு உரைபாண உய்த்து) in Ainthinai Ezhupathu 49. The image is common in marutham, but the change of addressee is specific and true.

Eyes reddened by the falls are shared (நீர் அலைச் சிவந்த ... கண்; பாய்ந்தருவி ஆடினேமாக ... சேந்தனவாம் சேயரிக்கண்). The concealment reading of Ainthinai Aimpathu 15 depends on an addressee the colophon does not give; ஆம் suggests an explanation but the 'safe to name' claim is inference.

Malaipadukadam sets the nameless dead (தம்பெயர் தம்மொடு கொண்டனர் மாய்ந்தோர்) as more than the sands of the Seyaru, and draws 'புகழொடுங் கழிக நம் வரைந்த நாள்': the Kural's only survivor measured against a vast forgetting. The uncertain line 552 does not affect the point.

இன்னே வருகுவர் தாயர் (Mullaippattu 16), overheard as virichi omen, against இன்னே வருவர் நமர் (Kar Narpathu 2), spoken by the lightning as his தூது. A near-verbatim formula moved from omen-rite to the season; the teaches is specific.

Both stop the man at departure, but Ainthinai Aimpathu 34's robbers on the road (கொலைபிரியா வன்கண்ணர் ஆறலைக்கும் அத்தம்) are the stock paalai road, and the poem still ends on the woman (வாள்தடங்கண் மாதரை நீத்து). The two-levers point is true but thin, and qualifies does not fit.

Both use the Bharata war (ஈரைம்பதின்மரும் பொருது களத்து ஒழிய; ஈரைம் பதின்மரும் பொருதுகளத் தவிய ... ஐவர் போல): one for the patron's food (பெருஞ்சோற்று மிகுபதம் வரையாது கொடுத்தோய்), one for his victory roar. The contrast of giving and conquest is real, but 'feeder of both sides' is not in Purananuru 2, which does not say to whom.

134 says her beauty came back with him (தான்வந் தன்றுஎன் மாமைக் கவினே); 137 asks the bard whether those who loved him regain their former beauty (பண்டைத் தந்நலம் பெறுபவோ). These are different moments of one decade, return and charge, not incompatible claims; the teaches itself reads them as a cycle, which is a qualification.

Paripadal 8 lists the rites (சாந்தம், புகை, விளக்கம், வீ) and this-world boons (கரு வயிறு உறுக, செய் பொருள் வாய்க்க, ஐ அமர் அடுக); Thiruppugazh 8 at Parangiri confesses their omission (பல மலர் கொடு ... பணிந்திலன், சிகரமும் வலம் வருகிலன்) and asks only for the hour of death. Same hill, rites inverted; the teaches holds.

369 is the friend urging the elopement (செல்வாம் தோழி), the pods rattling like anklets; 378 is the foster mother praying the road be shaded (ஞாயிறு காயாது ... தண்மழை தலைய ஆகுக). Neither claims the road is safe or dangerous against the other; both wish it well. Different voices in one drama are not a tension, and 'cannot both be right' is untrue.

நீடுவர் கொல் and நீடலர் share a verb, but நீடு is the commonest verb of delay in paalai, and the two poems are not an exchange. Saying 'the paalai exchange turned on a single verb' overstates a shared ordinary word.

Thinaimozhi 41's ஐயகொல் ஆன்றார் தொடர்பு does echo Kural 782's நீரவர் கேண்மை, and 'கண்டநாள் போலானான்' is a waning. But the poem uses the maxim against him rather than contradicting it, as the teaches itself says, so it is an application, not a tension. ஐய is ambiguous (slight, or wondrous), which the reading must assume.

Kuruntokai 190's bell rung at every step of the bull (நல்லேறு இயங்குதோறு இயம்பும்) does show her awake, and Kural 1168 says the night has only her for company. But the sleepless night is shared topic, and the bell's proof of wakefulness is all in Kuruntokai 190; the Kural's அளித்து (pity or scorn) is not engaged.

Akananuru 164 says only that she would regain her beauty 'வெஞ்சின வேந்தன் வினைவிடப் பெறினே', if the king released him; it does not say the king is reluctant. Ainkurunuru 467's report (நம்மினும் விரையும் என்ப) is compatible with that. Different poems and kings; the teaches' 'a report the camp itself contradicts' is not in the Tamil.

Kural 1183's exchange (கொண்டார் கைம்மாறா நோயும் பசலையும் தந்து) is turned in Kuruntokai 236 into a demand: 'தந்தனை சென்மோ ... நீ உண்ட என் நலனே'. The eaten beauty cannot be returned, so the demand argues against leaving; the teaches is specific.

Kural 882 fears the foe who seems kin (கேள்போல் பகைவர் தொடர்பு); Thirikadugam 4's item காய்வானைக் கைவாங்கிக் கோடல் fits only if முற்றன்னை is split முன் + தன்னை, which the marker flags as uncertain. Real but resting on one division of an ambiguous word.

Both have the heart go after the man (சென்றஎன் நெஞ்சே; பின்செல்வாய் பேதைஎன் நெஞ்சு). But Ainkurunuru 295 is union (it may settle there, அவணுறை மேவலின்) and Kural 1248 is separation with his grace withheld (நல்கார்), so the 'same act judged by how he answers' is a generalisation across different situations.

Purananuru 152 shows Ori's unguarded giving (ஓம்பா ஈகை) to a troupe in the wild; Natrinai 52 takes 'மா வள் ஓரி கை வளம் இயைவது ஆயினும்' as the most a man could gain and still finds it slight (ஐது ஏகு) against the embrace. A puram name used as a fixed measure in akam; the note says what the akam poet does with it.

Pakanrai and the cold season are shared, and Ainkurunuru 456 asks உள்ளார் கொல்லோ. But Akananuru 24 is a different poem in which the man sets his camp against her lonely nights; making it the answer to her question gives only the shared topic that both lovers suffer apart.

poems.note: The konrai mistaking the unseasonal rain is the friend's whole argument, not a hidden picture; striking it leaves nothing.
Thunder and lightning are given as drum and Death by open metaphor; no creature acts.

iraicchi.act: buries the old plantains to ripen for later
iraicchi.sense: the hill lord, having given his assurance, will come back to claim her as the monkey returns for what it laid by

iraicchi.act: brings grain from the ruined village to feed the hen tired after laying
iraicchi.sense: the man on the road will tend the girl as the cock tends his weak mate

poems.note: The salt-carters' clamour is joined to the gossip by கடுப்ப, an open comparison.
The pregnant monkey drawing honey with spring water may point to the heroine, but I cannot state in one sentence what it implies.
Pairs: the dune heaped by the wind as the talk that piles up, and the tall palm made short as the distance to exposure shortened (குறுகி / குறிய ஆகும்); a generous but two-point mapping.
The new flood is mapped to the woman part by part, but with the markers ஆக (அறல் ஆக, கயல் ஆக), so it is an open figure.

ullurai.anchor: நின் மாண் இழை மகளிரை எம் மனைத் தந்து

poems.note: Lines 1-3 are obscure (புண்கிடந்த புள்); I could not fix a carrier or vehicle.
The comparison is to a puram event, set out openly (ஆர்ப்பினும் பெரிதே).
The deer pair's cry (இரங்கும்) is a sound; it is close to the creature-pair case but no act beyond crying is given.
The verse is fragmentary; too little survives to apply either rule.

iraicchi.act: embraces its mate and suffers hunger rather than go to other lands
iraicchi.sense: he should stay with the girl rather than leave her for gain

iraicchi.act: calls in loneliness on the kalli branch thinking of the cock gone to seek food
iraicchi.sense: the man who left for gain must pass such a hen and still bear to live apart, which is her reproach
